stages.title: First words
stages.context: Stonewake’s trail beacons need clear messages. Start with names, text, input and conversion before changing their signals.

stages.title: Decisions on the trail
stages.context: A fork in the valley opens only when its condition is true. Read expressions first, then follow one branch.

stages.title: Repeat with a purpose
stages.context: The beacon patrol repeats its route. Track one iteration, then the stopping rule, before tracing nested loops.

stages.title: Small reliable programs
stages.context: Give the beacons reusable instructions. Follow arguments and returns, then diagnose names, scope and invalid input.

stages.title: Pack and count
stages.context: The company needs a supply list in Thornveil. Learn where an item lives before changing or searching the pack.

stages.title: Change the supplies
stages.context: Add supplies, remove used items and take slices. Notice which methods change the list and which return a value.

stages.title: Share without surprises
stages.context: Two companions may be holding the same list. Compare aliases, copies and independent rows before estimating access cost.

stages.title: Build and preserve records
stages.context: Filter a new supply list, then use tuples for fixed records. A tuple can still refer to a mutable list.

stages.title: Prepare the workbench
stages.context: Emberglow’s workshop trays are out of order. Review list updates, iteration and their cost before writing a sorting pass.

stages.title: Bubble Sort
stages.context: Neighbouring tray labels can trade places. Trace one pass, keep its bounds safe, then explain stability and early exit.

stages.title: Insertion Sort
stages.context: Keep one sorted tray and insert the next label into it. Save the key before shifting items and test nearly sorted input.

stages.title: Selection Sort and comparison
stages.context: Select the smallest remaining label for each position. Compare swaps, comparisons, stability and Python’s key-based sorting.

stages.title: Unique gate permits
stages.context: At Oathforge, use the loops, list operations and functions learned on the road to repair the Castellan’s records. Oathforge’s gate accepts each permit once. Use sets to track membership and combine groups of permitted travellers.

stages.title: Named workshop records
stages.context: At Oathforge, use the loops, list operations and functions learned on the road to repair the Castellan’s records. The Castellan guards records indexed by names. Read and update dictionaries, handle missing keys and choose hashable keys.

stages.title: Reuse the workshop instructions
stages.context: At Oathforge, use the loops, list operations and functions learned on the road to repair the Castellan’s records. Split the keep’s repair instructions into modules and functions. Then examine default arguments and lazy iteration.

stages.title: Objects and recovery
stages.context: At Oathforge, use the loops, list operations and functions learned on the road to repair the Castellan’s records. Model separate gate devices with instances. Recover from bad input and close files correctly before confronting their guardian.

stages.title: Undo a wrong turn
stages.context: The catacombs repeat their corridors. A stack remembers the latest turn first: push, pop, undo and bracket matching.

stages.title: Serve in arrival order
stages.context: The old prison’s service bells form a queue. Follow FIFO, use deque efficiently, then distinguish a priority queue.

stages.title: Find the missing route
stages.context: Search the corridor register one entry at a time. Only after confirming sorted order should you discard half a search range.

stages.title: Choose a search strategy
stages.context: Compare search tradeoffs with the sorting ideas from Emberglow. Finish by choosing a stack or queue for an actual route task.

stages.title: Follow the chain
stages.context: The castle approach is a broken chain of watch posts. A node stores a value and a link; walk the links to count or search.

stages.title: Repair the links
stages.context: Reconnect the drawbridge messages. Insert and delete carefully, including an empty chain and the final node.

stages.title: Reverse and detect loops
stages.context: The old escape route runs backwards and one branch loops. Preserve the next link while reversing; use slow and fast pointers for cycles.

stages.title: Compare route structures
stages.context: At the outer gate, compare sentinels, two-way links and sorted chains. Decide when an indexed array makes repeated searches easier.

stages.title: Return from each room
stages.context: The inner keep repeats smaller versions of its halls. Find a base case, make progress, return to the caller and reuse repeated answers.

stages.title: Read a branching floor plan
stages.context: A corridor branches into rooms without circling back: a rooted tree. Identify leaves, edges and height before choosing an order.

stages.title: Visit every room
stages.context: Preorder, inorder, postorder and level order visit the same rooms differently. Trace the walk before comparing its cost.

stages.title: Keep the keys searchable
stages.context: The keep orders keys in a BST. Search, insert and remove them, then see why an unbalanced tree can become a chain.

stages.title: Balance the throne locks
stages.context: The throne passage uses height-balanced search trees. Start with the BST rule and balance factors before attempting a repair.

stages.title: Rebalance after insertion
stages.context: A new key can lean a subtree left or right. Identify LL, RR, LR or RL before performing the matching rotation.

stages.title: Preserve and repair the tree
stages.context: Every rotation must preserve all links and update heights. Deletion may shrink a subtree and require another repair above it.
